story.fullStory:
Gap Band's "Burn Rubber On Me" — original release 1967. "Burn Rubber (Why You Wanna Hurt Me)" is an American funk song originally performed by the Gap Band in 1980 and written by member Charlie Wilson, Rudy Taylor, and producer Lonnie Simmons.

Chart performance
In 1981, it peaked at number 84 on the Billboard Hot 100, number 90 on Cash Box and number 1 on the R&B charts.

Billboard magazine ranked it as the 12th biggest R&B single of 1981.

"Burn Rubber (Why You Wanna Hurt Me)" is an American funk song originally performed by the Gap Band in 1980 and written by member Charlie Wilson, Rudy Taylor, and producer Lonnie Simmons.

Background According to engineer Jack Rouben, the foundation of the song started with its bassline: "[The track] was a musical idea that Charlie came up with on the Minimoog that turned into a groove, then a completed arrangement, and then they put the lyrics at the very end...This song was built upon that one repeating bass track, and that was the jam that blossomed into a whole complete song." Rouben also remarked how the title for this song, along with many other hits by the band, was a phrase coined by co-writer Rudy Taylor.

Since their inception in 1967, the Gap Band has released 15 studio albums, 12 compilation albums and 2 live albums.

The Gap Band was an American R&B and funk band that rose to fame during the 1970s and 1980s.
The band consisted of three brothers: Charlie, Ronnie, and Robert Wilson, along with other members.
The band was originally named The Greenwood, Archer, and Pine Band after streets (Greenwood, Archer, and Pine) in the historic Greenwood neighborhood in the brothers' hometown of Tulsa, Oklahoma.
